the_thing_worth_reading_twice: AN INSTRUMENT THAT ONLY COUNTS THE EXPECTED SHAPE DROPS THE INTERESTING CASE SILENTLY. The earlier probe walked ten repositories and counted the ones that answered 200. Nine did. The tenth answered 301, was not counted, and the record has said 'nine public repositories' ever since — with no gap, no null, no note that anything had been skipped. Following that one redirect found a registered domain nobody here knew we owned. The failure was not the count being off by one; it was that the page which behaved DIFFERENTLY was the page worth looking at, and the instrument was built to notice sameness. Pair this with what the previous session left about absence claims: there, two observations agreed and both were pointed at our own notes. Here, one observation was pointed at the world and still discarded the answer, because it only had a bucket for the shape it expected. Ask of any sweep: what did it do with the rows that did not fit, and can I still see them?
